title: Why Is My Refrigerator Making a Clicking Noise?

seo.title: Why Is My Refrigerator Making a Clicking Noise?
seo.meta_description: An occasional click can be normal when relays, valves, or defrost controls change state.
seo.search_intent: Identify the likely causes of “why is my refrigerator making a clicking noise,” use observable clues to decide what to check first, and know when the problem is no longer basic household troubleshooting.

excerpt: An occasional click can be normal when relays, valves, or defrost controls change state. Repeated clicking with failed startup attempts or poor cooling points to a different problem.
content_html:
An occasional click can be normal when relays, valves, or defrost controls change state. Repeated clicking with failed startup attempts or poor cooling points to a different problem.

Match the click to refrigerator behavior

If it clicks and continues operating normally, it may be a control switching. If click-click accompanies a short hum and shutdown, note that cycle.

Check for stable power

A loose receptacle, unsuitable power strip, or poor supply can affect startup. The refrigerator should be connected as the manufacturer specifies, typically directly to a suitable outlet.

Listen for attempted compressor starts

Repeated clicking from the compressor area with little or no cooling can involve the start device, overload protector, or compressor. Internal diagnosis requires service.

Disconnect for burning odor or abnormal heat

Clicking accompanied by electrical odor, smoke, or a hot plug should not be ignored. Stop use and arrange inspection before powering it again.
